72db8fb6b2d75761: TAIPEI: China's Xi Jinping told President Donald Trump on Thursday that he hoped the US will adhere to the "correct position" of opposing Taiwan independence, and that the Chinese stance on "reunification" is clear-cut.
Below are some questions and answers about what is meant by the term "Taiwan independence" and the positions of the Chinese, US and Taiwanese governments.
WHAT IS TAIWAN'S HISTORY AND FORMAL NAME TODAY?
The Qing dynasty incorporated Taiwan as part of Fujian province in 1684 and only declared it a separate Chinese province in 1885.
Following the Qing's defeat in a war with Japan, it became a Japanese colony in 1895. In 1945, it was handed over to the Republic of China government at the end of World War Two.
In 1949 after being defeated by Mao Zedong's Communist forces, the Republic of China government fled and moved its capital to Taiwan, and Republic of China remains the island's formal name.
Mao set up the People's Republic of China, and claimed it was the only legitimate Chinese government for the whole of China, including Taiwan, as the Republic of China's successor state.
WHAT IS TAIWAN'S INTERNATIONAL STATUS AND CHINA'S POSITION?
For decades, the Republic of China in Taipei also claimed to be the legitimate Chinese government, but in 1971 Beijing took over the China seat at the United Nations from Taipei.
Most major Western countries and US allies maintain close unofficial ties with Taiwan by recognising the Republic of China passport and having de facto embassies in each other's capitals.

China says it will not renounce the use of force to bring Taiwan under its control. Beijing has offered Taiwan a "one country, two systems" model similar to Hong Kong, which promised the city a high degree of autonomy, although no major political party in Taiwan supports that.
WHAT IS THE US POSITION?
Any change in official US wording on Taiwan would upend decades of policy set by both Republican and Democratic presidents.

The US severed official ties with Taipei in favour of Beijing in 1979 but is bound by the Taiwan Relations Act to provide the island with the means to defend itself. The US officially takes no position on Taiwan's sovereignty under Washington's "One China" policy.
In 2022, the State Department also added wording on the Six Assurances, referring to six Reagan-era security assurances given to Taiwan, which the United States declassified in 2020.

Among the assurances made in 1982, but never previously formally made public, are statements that the US has not set a date for ending arms sales to Taiwan, nor agreed to prior consultation with Beijing on such sales, or to revise the Taiwan Relations Act that underpins US policy towards the island.
China has repeatedly demanded that the US end arms sales to Taiwan.

In May after meeting Xi in Beijing, Trump said he was still considering whether to go ahead with new weapons sales and that the US was "not looking to have somebody say, 'Let's go independent because the United States is backing us'."
The US ended its formal defence alliance with Taiwan in 1979 and has since then had a policy of "strategic ambiguity" on whether it would come to Taipei's defence should Beijing attack.
IS TAIWAN EFFECTIVELY ALREADY AN INDEPENDENT COUNTRY?

Taiwan, whose people elect their own leaders and whose government controls a defined area of territory with its own military, passport and currency, enjoys de facto independence even if that is not formally recognised by most countries.

Taiwan's government says the Republic of China is a sovereign state and that Beijing has no right to speak for or represent it given the People's Republic of China has no say in how it chooses its leaders and has never ruled Taiwan.
COULD TAIPEI DECLARE A "REPUBLIC OF TAIWAN"?
It would be very difficult and require parliamentary approval of a constitutional amendment and then a referendum, rather than a simple declaration by President Lai Ching-te.
At least 75% of lawmakers would need to pass that amendment, and the ruling Democratic Progressive Party and main opposition party the Kuomintang (KMT) currently have an equal number of seats.
The DPP, which has been in power since 2016, has not made an attempt to change the constitution. The KMT strongly opposes any attempts to change the name Republic of China.
WHAT DOES TAIWAN'S PRESIDENT SAY ABOUT INDEPENDENCE?

China detests Lai and calls him a "separatist." Before Lai was elected president he made comments about being a "practical worker for Taiwan independence." Lai maintains he simply meant Taiwan is already an independent country. - Reuters

f1131eb467c5f17a: KUALA LUMPUR: The risk of major flooding during the Melaka election, expected in November, is low, but monsoon surges must be monitored, a meteorologist says.

Universiti Malaya (UM) meteorologist Professor Emeritus Datuk Dr Azizan Abu Samah said November marked the start of the Northeast Monsoon, which generally brought more rain, but this did not necessarily mean flooding in Melaka.
He said weather conditions during the election would also be influenced by the El Niño phenomenon, which could reduce the risk of prolonged rain that could cause major flooding.
"November has already entered the Northeast Monsoon season. So, generally, it is the rainy season, although we are also influenced by El Niño.

"So, the risk of rainfall that could lead to major flooding is low. There may be flash floods, but if voters go to the polls in the morning, I do not think there will be much of an issue with rain," he said when contacted here today.
Last Tuesday, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh announced the dissolution of the Melaka state legislative assembly to pave the way for the 16th state election.
The Melaka state legislative assembly has 28 seats and its current term was originally scheduled to end on Dec 31.
Azizan said weather conditions would need to be monitored based on developments at the time, as monsoon surges might or might not occur on polling day.
"Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has extensive experience in monitoring and forecasting monsoon surges, enabling early warnings to be issued if such conditions are expected.
"Computerised forecasts by MetMalaysia on monsoon surges can provide an indication about four to seven days in advance.
"The forecast period for heavy rain is shorter and is generally more useful within about 48 to 72 hours before an event," he said.
He said monsoon surges could generally be detected several days in advance based on changes in atmospheric pressure systems, including the development of high pressure over Siberia and China.
"MetMalaysia's ability to forecast monsoon surges has also improved through years of monitoring the phenomenon," he said.
However, Azizan said it was still too early to determine the weather specifically on polling day as the election date had yet to be set.
"November is still some time away. We can give an indication of the season, but we cannot say when, where or what time it will rain," he said.
d6df4ac59bf829ec: KUALA LUMPUR: KEB Bhd has signed an underwriting agreement with M&A Securities Sdn Bhd ahead of its initial public offering (IPO) on the ACE Market.
The IPO comprises a public issue of 138.54 million new shares and an offer for sale of 88.24 million existing shares, totalling 226.78 million shares.

Of the public issue, 44.12 million shares, or five per cent of the company's enlarged share capital, will be allocated to the Malaysian public, while 22.06 million shares, or 2.5 per cent, are earmarked for eligible directors, employees and individuals who have contributed to the group's success.

Another 22.06 million shares, or 2.5 per cent, will be placed with Bumiputera investors, while the remaining 50.3 million shares, or 5.7 per cent, are reserved for private placement to selected investors.
KEB managing director Datuk Lim Kim Chong said the IPO marked an important step in strengthening the company's platform for future growth.

"It will support our plans to expand our development pipeline, acquire additional landbank and enhance our financial flexibility as we continue delivering value-accretive property developments," he said.
Proceeds from the public issue will be used for landbank acquisition, working capital for project development, repayment of bank borrowings and listing expenses.
M&A Equity Holdings Bhd's Datuk Bill Tan said KEB was well positioned to leverage the listing for its next phase of growth.
"We are pleased to formalise this underwriting agreement with KEB as the group advances towards its proposed ACE Market listing," he said.
KEB has more than two decades of experience in residential, industrial, commercial and mixed-use property development.
Its in-house construction arm, KEB Utama Sdn Bhd, is a CIDB Grade G7 registered contractor, allowing the group greater oversight of project execution, quality and delivery timelines.
KEB has completed 14 property development projects to date.
Its development pipeline comprises two ongoing projects with a combined estimated gross development value of RM773.29 million and four future projects worth an estimated RM940.74 million.

024ee267411a56a8: NAGOYA: Tomokazu Harimoto said Japan had overcome their inferiority complex after ending table tennis powerhouse China's 32-year run as Asian Games men's team champions in a nail-biting final.
China had won gold in the event at every Games since 1994 but they were dethroned by Japan after Sora Matsushima beat Wen Ruibo in the decisive match to win 3-2.
The Japan team also featured Harimoto, whose parents were both born in China and whose mother once represented the country at the world championships.
"That we beat them was proof that we had lacked confidence before," said Harimoto, whose sister Miwa plays for Japan's women's team.
"I'm happy, but looking at the actual contest, there was nothing unusual about the way we played or the outcome.
"We just managed to attain the one thing we'd been missing – confidence."
China's team featured world number one Wang Chuqin but his team-mates Lin Shidong and Wen are respectively ranked eighth and 15th in the world.
Japan had two top-five players in number three Matsushima and number four Harimoto.
"China used to have six or seven strong players, that's why their era lasted 10 or 20 years," said Harimoto.
"Now with two of us in the world top five, Matsushima and I can win like this."
Harimoto could not bring himself to watch the final match from the team bench after beating Wang to level it at 2-2.
"I thought it was better not to go back, a bit like a superstition," said Harimoto.
"If I was on the bench, Matsushima would see me. He probably wouldn't mind, but I minded."
Wang won the opening match against Matsushima but lost 3-0 against Harimoto.
The Chinese player said: "Psychologically, I ran into problems."
"Perhaps we panicked a little in trying to be better, and rushed some shots," he said.
China got their own back in the women's team final, beating Japan 3-0.
But the men's defeat left a bitter taste in the mouths of Chinese fans, who vented their anger on social media.
"The men's team, despite enjoying the best resources and treatment, suffers from lack of continuity and a talent gap," one user wrote on Weibo.
"There is no one coming through," wrote another. - AFP

1d88ac566e14bcc0: KUALA LUMPUR: Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) is targeting RM15 billion in green and transition asset investments by 2030, building on the RM8.1 billion already invested as it strengthens its sustainability agenda.
The country's largest fund manager is also targeting RM500 million in social investments under its enhanced Sustainability Framework 2026 (SF 2026).
SF 2026 sets 16 measurable environmental, social and governance (ESG) targets across its investments, operations and stewardship activities.
PNB said SF 2026 builds on its 2022 sustainability framework and aims to strengthen long-term resilience while ensuring that the value created from Malaysians' savings benefits future generations.
Under SF 2026, PNB has identified three strategic anchors: story pension WISHadvancing organisational sustainability, responsible stewardship and strengthening the nation-building agenda.
Under organisational sustainability, PNB will maintain net-zero Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, while working towards its longer-term aspiration of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050.
It will also seek to reduce indirect emissions from business travel, strengthen sustainable procurement and improve accessibility and inclusivity across its premises and services.

For responsible stewardship, PNB will focus on portfolio decarbonisation, climate resilience, nature and biodiversity, as well as fair and equitable employment practices, including labour and living wage principles.
PNB said these measures are intended to strengthen the resilience and long-term competitiveness of companies in which Malaysians' savings are invested.
The third anchor, strengthening the nation-building agenda, focuses on social and financial inclusion and social investment.
Initiatives will include talent development, scholarships, community investment, financial literacy and heritage preservation.
PNB president and group chief executive Datuk Rizal Rickman Ramli said the new framework represents a continuation of the sustainability work undertaken since 2022.

"Sustainability has always been integral to how PNB fulfils its mandate. When we introduced our sustainability framework in 2022, we made a deliberate commitment to turn our sustainability ambitions into measurable action.
"Now, we have progressively achieved eight of the 10 targets we set and made meaningful progress across our broader sustainability agenda," he said.
Among the milestones, PNB said it achieved its Net Zero Enterprise 2025 target, with 100 per cent of its electricity use supported by renewable energy certificates for PNB Enterprise.
It has also invested RM8.1 billion in green and transition assets.
Rizal said SF 2026 was "not a reset, but a progression", with greater emphasis on responsible investment, long-term stewardship, social impact and nation building.

"As an institution entrusted with the savings of millions of Malaysians, we must ensure that the value we create endures across generations, while contributing to a more resilient, inclusive and sustainable Malaysia," he said.

PNB said the framework reflects its approach of linking responsible investment with broader economic and social outcomes, including stronger businesses, economic opportunities, financial inclusion and social development.
The framework is anchored by the statement "Investing Responsibly, Empowering Generations" and includes commitments extending to 2030 and beyond.

eccf19f7a91e5e50: SEREMBAN, Sept 25 — Former Negeri Sembilan menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has called on current Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to specify the alleged shortcomings of the previous administration that led to issues involving the state’s customary traditions and royal institution.

Aminuddin said the public had the right to know what actions were allegedly not taken during his tenure as Menteri Besar, including the specific provisions of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan (UUTKNS) 1959 that were allegedly breached and when the alleged violation occurred.
"What actions were said to have been overlooked? Which provisions of the UUTKNS 1959 were allegedly breached and when did the alleged breach occur?

"If there was an offence, state clearly what it was. If there was a violation of the law, identify the relevant provision. On an issue of this magnitude, the public deserves clear and verifiable facts,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Aminuddin said he was prepared to take responsibility for decisions made during his tenure as Menteri Besar by providing relevant documents, dates and legal provisions based on official records.
Yesterday, Ismail said the issue in the state did not stem from the current administration but was a problem inherited from the previous government.

Meanwhile, the Port Dickson Member of Parliament also questioned Ismail’s decision to sign a proclamation document related to the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, despite previously choosing not to sign the same document.
Aminuddin said the proclamation document dated April 19 was presented to him on April 20 while he was still Menteri Besar, for his signature under Article 10(2) of the UUTKNS 1959.

"I decided not to sign the document. If I, as Menteri Besar at the time, could make that decision due to doubts over the process, how could the signature of the next Menteri Besar appear on the same document?

"Datuk Ismail, with his legal background, would certainly understand the importance of the process. The issue involving Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir is about whether the process was properly followed or had flaws from the beginning,” he said.

Aminuddin said Article 10 of the UUTKNS 1959 not only covers matters relating to the powers concerning the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar, but also sets out procedures that must be fulfilled, including matters related to a full and complete inquiry. — Bernama
24f05cc3a7321849: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — The Negeri Sembilan government has notified the Conference of Rulers of Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar’s selection as the state’s 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar, according to an Undang and three ruling chiefs whose positions are disputed.

The group said the notification meant Tunku Nadzaruddin was the only person with lawful authority to perform the functions of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959, including attending meetings of the Conference of Rulers, The Star reported today.
It also urged the state administration to recognise Tunku Nadzaruddin and provide him with the privileges and entitlements attached to the office.
“The state government administration must comply and remain loyal and must not commit any act of disobedience.
“The state government administration must also immediately accord all privileges and entitlements prescribed for Tunku Nadzaruddin,” they said.
State civil servants, meanwhile, were urged to follow decisions of the executive council and not bow to pressure from any party.
The group said the official notification to the Conference of Rulers reflected its position that Tunku Nadzaruddin was entitled to exercise all the functions of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.

“Through the... official notification to the Conference of Rulers, only Tunku Nadzaruddin... has the lawful authority to exercise all functions of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959, including attending all meetings of the Conference of Rulers,” they said.

The joint statement was issued by Undang of Johol Datuk Muhammed Abdullah, Datuk Mubarak Thahak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad and Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin, whose positions as the Undang of Sungei Ujong, Jelebu and Rembau respectively are disputed.
Tunku Besar Tampin Tunku Syed Razman Syed Idrus Al-Qadri was also a signatory.
The group maintains that Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir was removed as Yang di-Pertuan Besar on April 19, with Tunku Nadzaruddin subsequently chosen as his successor.
The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang disputes that account, maintaining that Tuanku Muhriz remains the lawful Yang di-Pertuan Besar and that the April 19 proclamation was invalid.

6c1e4ff7abb3e9ed: KUALA LUMPUR: When Malaysia's rhythmic gymnasts take to the mat at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, they will compete in a new format that requires "collective thinking".
In a format change aligned with the Olympics, the Olympic Council of Asia has replaced the traditional individual team with the five-gymnast group all-around event.
In the previous individual team format, solo routines were combined for a total score.
Carrying Malaysia's challenge in this new format are Maia Ong Xiao Han, Carol Na Yuan Qi, Bernice See Qin Nin, Victoria Manalang Tan Fu-Hui and Low Ee Shuen.
This will present a difficult tactical test as building synchronicity in group gymnastics usually takes years. But this Malaysian quintet have only been together for months.

The squad underwent significant changes following last year's SEA Games in Thailand. Ee Shuen, 17, was promoted from the junior ranks only this year, while Victoria stepped into the starting five alongside veterans Maia, Bernice, and team captain Carol.

In group rhythmic gymnastics, where an apparatus throw missed by centimetres can ruin an entire routine, instinctive teamwork is essential. That reality was made clear at the Asian Championships in Tashkent in May, where the newly combined Malaysian team finished seventh in the group all-around.
With only the top eight teams advancing to the final at the Asian Games, the Malaysian squad find themsleves right on the qualification cutline.
National team manager Foong Peik Chow said forging that collective instinct has been their priority under Japanese coach Eriko Akebayashi.
"I would say the team have improved technically and are mentally prepared for this level of competition. All five gymnasts must think as one to give a good routine," Peik Chow said.
"The coach (Akebayashi) has worked on the accuracy of the exchanges, collaboration, and body difficulties," Peik Chow added.
The competition will be staged at the Nippon Gaishi Hall in Nagoya from Oct 1 to 3, where Malaysia will perform two routines — one featuring five balls and a mixed routine of hoops and ribbons.
Malaysia have never won an Asian Games medal in rhythmic gymnastics. The best result was a fourth place in the individual team event at Doha 2006.

"To be in the finals is our target. We hope to still be the best among the Southeast Asian countries. Of course, we still work towards breaking into the top five countries at the Asian level of competition," Peik Chow added.
d042dcf6db4b4180: LONDON: Carlos Alcaraz has had enough of pulling all-nighters at Grand Slams, urging organisers to finish play by 11pm after his US Open title defence came to an end in a gruelling 3.33am finish earlier this month.
Ben Shelton beat Alcaraz in the quarter-finals of the US Open in the latest-ever finish at the year's final Grand Slam.

Prior to that, three matches ended after 2 am during the tournament's opening week, while two more ran well beyond midnight, and Venus Williams was involved in the latest-starting clash that began at 12.13am.
"I think it's too much," seven-time Grand Slam champion Alcaraz told reporters in London on Thursday ahead of the Laver Cup.
"The last match people stayed, but if that match had been played earlier, the court could have been packed.
"I would like to change the schedule a little with a maximum finish at 11pm, or whatever would be better."

The US Tennis Association, which organises the US Open, did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment outside regular business hours, but the body has said it will evaluate scheduling options in the future.
Other Grand Slams have taken action to curb late finishes, with Wimbledon halting play under an 11pm local curfew and the French Open limiting night sessions to one match.
The issue has gained traction amid a broader pushback by top players over working conditions, including a packed competitive calendar.
Agassi wants guaranteed downtime for players
Andre Agassi, captain of Team World at the Laver Cup, stressed the need for guaranteed downtime at the end of the season.

"It would be my hope (for) an off-season of some relative form of security for both the players and also for the fans so that they look forward to the game," the eight-times Grand Slam champion told reporters.
"I think in a lot of cases, tennis would benefit from that."

Asked about where the Laver Cup, which is named after Australian great Rod Laver and borders on being an exhibition event, fits into the tennis schedule, Agassi replied, "I think this is a fantastic event.
"I'd hate to see the compromise ever come on an event like this that is hosted under such a magnificent name and person that none of us would be here today without in this game.
"So this wouldn't be the place I would choose to cut some edges. But I would like to see these awesome athletes always be at their best. I think everybody wins with that."
2927eb32dfef0e03: KUALA LUMPUR: Suruhanjaya Pilihan Raya Malaysia (SPR) akan mengadakan mesyuarat khas bagi urusan PRN Melaka ke-16, pada 7 Okt.

a6e970b915fc55d4: NAGOYA: Malaysia ended a 36-year wait for the men's sepak takraw team regu gold medal after beating traditional rivals Thailand 2-0 in the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games final at Nagoya City Mizuho Arena on Friday.
The victory matched Malaysia's achievement at the 1990 Beijing Asian Games, when they last won the event by defeating Thailand in the final.
Malaysia made a strong start as Mohammad Syahir Rosdi, Farhan Adam and Azlan Alias beat Thailand's Marukin Phanmakon, Putawan Sopa and Pornthep Tingbangbon 15-9, 5-15, 15-11 to take the opening tie.
Zulkifli Abd Razak, Aidil Aiman Azwawi and Afifudin Razali then sealed the gold with a 15-13, 15-10 win over Kritsanapong Nontakote, Tanaphon Sapyen and Wuttinu Kamsanor.
It was Malaysia's second consecutive victory over Thailand in a team regu final at a multi-sport Games, following their triumph at the Thailand SEA Games last December.
The win gave Malaysia their fourth gold medal of the Aichi-Nagoya Games.

c7069306e91bd801: SAN JOSE (California): Google will launch a prototype satellite to evaluate how its artificial intelligence (AI) chips perform in space, the company said on Thursday, reported German Press Agency (dpa).
"In low Earth orbit, satellites can access near-constant sunlight, generating up to eight times more solar power than on Earth," Google said in a blog post.
"Eventually, it could be possible to link together multiple constellations of satellites, allowing them to manage larger AI workloads while in orbit."

Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) will be loaded onto a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket next week to test how they handle the "physical stress of spaceflight and the radiation and thermal extremes of space", Google said.
"Some things can only be tested in space ... This first launch is about seeing what works, identifying points of failure, and applying those findings to future missions."
Cooling orbital data centres and ensuring that the satellites can communicate at very high bandwidth over extremely short distances are also "engineering hurdles", the company said.

"Exploring space as a viable location for scalable AI compute won't happen all at once. It takes methodical engineering, starting with proving our hardware can handle the physical and unpredictable realities of operating in orbit." — BERNAMA
48e9d0b7178cc85d: JERUSALEM: Israel's army said Friday that two reserve soldiers were killed in Gaza, with a military source telling AFP they died in an explosion of an Israeli army drone.
"The IDF drone crashed at a military post in the Gaza Strip but did not explode. The soldiers approached the drone, which exploded moments later," the official said.
"The incident is under review," the source added.
The army identified the soldiers as Nadav Kali, aged 24, and Ofek Moalem, 23, from its 7007th Battalion, 16th Brigade.

The deaths bring the number of Israeli soldiers killed in Gaza to 970 since the start of the war, which was launched in response to the Hamas attacks against Israel on Oct 7, 2023, that killed more than 1,200 people.
Of the 970 soldiers killed, seven have died since the start of a ceasefire last year.
The war waged by Israel in Gaza has left nearly 74,000 dead, according to the territory's health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
57f619778b16765c: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has struck out a suit by a man seeking a declaration that he is a Sikh and had never professed Islam, ruling that the matter falls within the jurisdiction of the shariah court.

A three-member bench led by Justice Firuz Jaffril unanimously allowed an appeal by the Federal Territories Islamic religious council (MAIWP) and the government, holding that the civil court had no jurisdiction to hear Shehzad Malik Sarwar Malik's challenge to his religious status.
Firuz, sitting with Justices Faizah Jamaludin and Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, said official documents showed that Shehzad was born in 1996 to parents who had voluntarily embraced Islam.

"The respondent came to court knowing that he was born a Muslim based on the documents and pursuant to Section 2 of the Administration of Islamic Law (Federal Territories) Act 1993 (Act 505)," Firuz said in his broad grounds.
The provision defines who is regarded as a Muslim under the Act. Firuz said the documents also legally identified Shehzad as a person professing Islam.
"Given the facts, this can be construed as renunciation and the case falls within the jurisdiction of the shariah court," he said.
He said the Court of Appeal was bound by the Federal Constitution and judicial precedents.
"The respondent could not come to the civil court as it did not have the jurisdiction to grant the orders sought," he said.
The bench made no order as to costs against Shehzad.
Shehzad filed an originating summons in December 2023 seeking a declaration that he was a practising Sikh and had never professed Islam.
He said although his parents were Muslims when he was born in June 1996, his mother, who has since died, raised him as a Sikh.
He said after his mother’s death in 2007, he was raised by his maternal uncle, who also practised Sikhism.

Shehzad also sought an order for the national registration department to amend his religious status from Islam to Sikhism, and change his name from Shehzad Malik bin Muhammad Sarwar Malik to Bilawal Singh Bhutter.
MAIWP argued that a Muslim mother could not convert her Muslim child to Sikhism, while the government said Shehzad had identified himself as a Muslim when applying for his identity card.
Last year, the High Court dismissed applications by MAIWP and the government to strike out Shehzad’s suit, finding that there were triable issues that should be determined at trial.
However, before the Court of Appeal, MAIWP lawyer Ahmad Kamal Abu Bakar, assisted by Arik Zakri Abdul Kadir, argued that the civil suit was unsustainable and should be struck out.
He said Shehzad’s remedy lay with the shariah court.
Senior federal counsel Husniyyah Hanapi supported the submission, pointing to Shehzad’s birth certificate and identity card, which recorded him as a Muslim.
Shehzad’s lawyer, Sachpreetraj Singh, assisted by Amanda Sonia Mathew, argued that a trial was necessary to determine whether he had ever been a Muslim in the first place.
He said the case was an ab initio challenge, meaning Shehzad’s position was that he had never been a Muslim from the outset.
"That is why we are here in the civil court, because it is our position that this is an ab initio case," he said.
649cd3ce9b0e1255: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Negeri Sembilan’s four undangs and the Tunku Besar of Tampin have called on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) to refrain from intervening in the state’s affairs, particularly those involving their constitutional prerogatives.

In a press conference in Seremban today, the group said Articles 10 and 11 of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959 vested the Undang Yang Empat with exclusive authority to appoint and remove the state ruler, Free Malaysia Today reported.
They also cautioned Anwar against using federal agencies in ways that could disrupt the administration of Negeri Sembilan.
“Do not overstep your bounds or intrude where you are not wanted. Do not sow disorder in our state using federal government agencies to paralyse the state government.

“Do not, merely for political gain or influence, or by yielding to pressure from certain quarters, act without reason and conscience, and in doing so violate the principle of constitutional supremacy.
“Do not act beyond your authority and interfere in matters that do not concern you,” they said.

The group said any action they considered unconstitutional would amount to a breach of the prime minister’s oath under the Sixth Schedule of the Federal Constitution, as well as a breach of trust under Article 71(1) and (2) and the principle of federalism.

They also turned their attention to outside parties, especially opposition political parties, warning them against “fishing in muddied waters” or “twisting the facts” through disparaging remarks about the state government and adat, or customs.

“No political party has the power to remove any ruler,” they said. “That power is vested solely in its rightful authority, and in the context of Negeri Sembilan, it falls within the power of the Undang Yang Empat.”
The group said Negeri Sembilan’s customs had been practised for more than 500 years and maintained that their role as custodians of those traditions gave them the best understanding of them.
“Only the jeweller knows the gem,” they said.
They further maintained that selecting and removing the Yang di-Pertuan Besar was a customary prerogative protected by Articles 7, 10 and 11 of the state constitution.

The undangs also rejected claims that Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim and the state executive council were responsible for Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir’s purported removal, describing the allegation as “malicious slander” driven by the personal interests of certain groups.
According to them, Ismail and the exco members were only fulfilling their constitutional obligation to act on the undangs’ decision under Article 10.

The statement came from Undang of Johol Datuk Muhammed Abdullah and was jointly issued with Datuk Mubarak Dohak, Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad and Abdul Rahim Yasin, whose positions as the Undangs of Sungei Ujong, Jelebu and Rembau are disputed.
The statement follows Anwar’s criticism on Wednesday of Ismail and the former exco over several issues concerning the royal institution that had become contentious in the state.

The exco had earlier, on September 16, said Tuanku Muhriz’s removal as Yang di-Pertuan Besar in April was legitimate and declared Tunku Nadzaruddin the new ruler of Negeri Sembilan, with Ismail endorsing the position the following day.
The state’s Dewan Keadilan dan Undang subsequently disputed that position, saying the exco’s decision carried no legal effect and that Tuanku Muhriz remained the legitimate Yang di-Pertuan Besar.

The dispute intensified on September 17 when the AGC said the proclamation seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz as Yang di-Pertuan Besar was invalid, rejecting it alongside the exco’s subsequent endorsement of the proclamation.
The AGC also said the menteri besar and the exco members at the time could not act on their own to remove the state ruler.
Three days later, Tuanku Muhriz withdrew the appointments of all 10 exco members, with breaches of their oaths of office cited as the reason.
dbaa7b00ea49671e: PETALING JAYA: Ketua Penerangan PKR Melaka, Eddiarman Mohd Yunos, berkata satu poster tular janaan kecerdasan buatan (AI) yang mengandungi beberapa kesilapan bukan siaran rasmi parti itu atau Pakatan Harapan (PH).

d52584a43d34259c: KUALA LUMPUR: Four locations in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 2pm, with Serian recording the highest reading at 174.
After weeks of choking haze affecting the country, Sarawak was the only state with areas in the unhealthy category.
The Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System showed Kuching recorded 162, followed by Samarahan at 161 and Sri Aman at 156.
Elsewhere, Bukit Rambai in Melaka recorded a reading at 90, followed by Sarikei at 87, Bintulu at 86, and Larkin in Johor and Kapit at 85 each.
In the Klang Valley, Shah Alam recorded 83, Johan Setia 80 and Cheras 78, all within the moderate range.
Three areas recorded good air quality: Tanah Merah in Kelantan at 46, Langkawi in Kedah at 38 and Besut in Terengganu at 30.
An API reading of 0 to 50 is considered good, 51 to 100 moderate and 101 to 200 unhealthy.
d4646977d5620fab: KUALA LUMPUR: The sessions court heard today that then Petronas manager Khairul Akmal Jasni expressed his intention to join Petros in a work email to two of the company’s senior officers in June 2024.

Petronas human resources (finance and risk) manager Suhaidah Labu, 42, said that apart from Khairul’s message, which read, "I look forward to joining your team", the email allegedly contained Petronas’s "Q1 2024 Upstream Business Performance – Operational and Financial" report dated May 10, 2024.
She said the email was addressed to Petros CFO Azha Jalil Abdul Jalil and CEO Janin Girie.
Suhaidah was testifying as the sixth prosecution witness in the trial of Khairul, who is accused of attempting to disclose a confidential Petronas document to Petros.
She said the email was shown to her by Petronas industrial relations officers Jumsuri Basri and Zatil Ismah Azmi on Dec 6, 2024, to confirm whether Khairul had resigned from the company.
"There was no record of his resignation (in the system) and he was still an active Petronas employee," she said in her witness statement.
However, during cross-examination by Khairul’s lawyer Louis Liaw, Suhaidah said she was unsure who had actually sent the email to Petros’s senior officers.
Liaw: Based on the email, you concluded that it was sent by Khairul Akmal?
Liaw: But you do not know who actually wrote the email and hit the send button?
In her witness statement, Suhaidah also said Khairul had verbally expressed his intention to be transferred to Sarawak where his family lived.
When questioned by deputy public prosecutor Noor Syafina Radzuan, Suhaidah said his request was not fulfilled as there was no vacant position for him in Sarawak.
Regarding Khairul's work performance at Petronas, Suhaidah said he performed exceptionally well and was regarded as a top talent within the company’s finance fraternity.
She said Khairul had in-depth knowledge and understanding of the factors influencing oil and gas prices.
Khairul is charged with attempting to disclose the document, which he allegedly obtained during his tenure at Petronas, to Petros.
The offence was allegedly committed at B-6-10, Marc Service Residence, Jalan Pinang, Dang Wangi, between 3.19pm and 3.21pm on June 8, 2024.
He was charged under Section 203A(1) read with Section 511 of the Penal Code, which carries a minimum fine of RM1 million, imprisonment of up to one year or both, upon conviction.
The trial before judge Mazuliana Abdul Rashid continues on Nov 18.

54f35833abf97664: SEOUL: MAMAMOO's Hwasa has set the internet abuzz following her performance at Brazil's Rock in Rio 2026.

dc9546d79a0fb575: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — As the Halloween season approaches, Nights of Fright is set to live up to its name as the annual horror event officially returned today for its 12th edition at Sunway Lagoon.
Since its inception in 2013, the festival has become a major annual horror attraction, featuring multiple walk-through haunted houses with original narratives, special effects, and live scare actors.
Over the years, zombies, vampires, mutants and killer clowns have taken over the festival grounds, giving visitors plenty of reasons to keep their eyes open.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Sunway Theme Parks general manager of business and marketing development Michelle Soong (centre left) and The Sudden Impact! Entertainment Company founder and global creative director as well as Nights of Fright creative director Lynton V. Harris (centre right) launch the 12th edition of Nights of Fright at Sunway Lagoon September 24, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Ape-ocalypse theme for 12th edition
This year’s event, titled Nights of Fright 12: Ape-ocalypse, is centred on a dystopian setting where primates have taken over the festival grounds and humans are hunted by chainsaw-wielding apes.

Lynton V. Harris, founder and global creative director of The Sudden Impact! Entertainment Company and creative director of Nights of Fright, said the theme draws inspiration from the Planet of the Apes and Mad Max film franchises.
He said the wider attraction line-up incorporates different horror and pop-culture genres, visual styles and cultural influences.
Sunway Theme Parks general manager of business and marketing development Michelle Soong said the Ape-ocalypse concept provides a new creative direction for this year’s event.
“The wider line-up allows us to bring together international influences with elements that are familiar and meaningful to audiences in Malaysia and the region,” she said.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Horror-themed puppets are seen at the launch of Nights of Fright 12 at Sunway Lagoon September 24, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Nine horror attractions from classic slashers, pontianak, yokai and K-pop horror
Malaysian and Asian storytelling, drawing from Japanese folklore, cult horror, twisted fairytales, manga and K-pop culture, takes centre stage across the haunted houses.
The nine horror attractions each present a distinct concept.
The main attraction, Ape-ocalypse: The Kingdom Kong, puts visitors in a world overrun by human-sized apes wielding chainsaws and ready to chase through the darkness.
Malaysian horror takes the spotlight in Pontianak vs Pocong, a short film screening set inside a haunted theatre where many can expect more than just sitting still.
Visitors entering the Yokai Road attraction will encounter yokai, the supernatural spirits, and uncanny phenomena from Japanese folklore, including the kappa and tengu.

The Freezer: Fresh Meat is set inside a grim and chilling human meat-processing facility, while Little Shop of Horrors brings the classic horror-comedy film about a carnivorous plant to life through a manga-inspired UV 3D experience.
Horrorwood: Wax Museum of Monsters brings visitors face-to-face with classic slasher icons from Hollywood, including Art the Clown from the Terrifier films and Ghostface from the Scream franchise.

The Not-So-Wonderful Wizard of Oz gives the classic fairytale a dark and twisted horror treatment, while Return to Silent Hill offers a psychological and atmospheric survival-horror experience inspired by the video game series.
Lastly, Romeos and Juliet: Jealousy, Obsession, Murder presents a macabre, blood-soaked take on the tragic romance, with a darker K-pop-inspired twist.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Visitors await the start of Nights of Fright 12: Ape-ocalypse at Sunway Lagoon September 24, 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Scare zones and other activities
In addition to the nine main attractions, Nights of Fright 12 has three scare zones where roaming performers and characters will interact with visitors around the park.
It will also feature 11 selected Sunway Lagoon rides transformed with horror themes during the event.
As part of a continuing tradition, the event will round off the evening with entertainment after dark featuring live performances on the main stage.
Soong said the event’s focus remained on immersive experiences as it returned for its 12th edition.
“Nights of Fright has always been about elevating immersion experiences and energising a movement that dominates the entertainment landscape in this region,” she said.
Nights of Fright 12 runs every Friday, Saturday and Sunday from September 25 to November 7, 2026.
Ticketing information is available through Klook and the Sunway Lagoon official webstore.
255a0e348c1eb75a: PUCHONG: 'Kebolehaksesan' merupakan unsur penting dalam reka bentuk sesuatu kemudahan, misalnya sistem pengumuman melalui pembesar suara untuk memudahkan urusan pengguna.
Penerangan audio begitu lazim dalam kehidupan seharian sehingga kita mungkin tidak menyedari bahawa cara maklumat disampaikan itu tidak dapat diakses oleh semua orang, khususnya golongan pekak.

Jurubahasa isyarat Wan Zuraidah Abu menyedari jurang kebolehaksesan maklumat ini ketika mengiringi sekumpulan atlet OKU di Hentian Puduraya. Mereka hampir terlepas bas selepas platform untuk perjalanan mereka ditukar dan pengumuman mengenainya hanya disampaikan melalui pembesar suara.
"Mereka tidak menyedari segala yang berlaku di sekeliling mereka," kata presiden Persatuan Jurubahasa Isyarat Malaysia ini kepada FMT.
"Saya beritahu mereka, 'platform kita tunggu bas tu kan dia dah tukar tau. Jadi kita kena pergi kat tempat yang dekat dengan platform'.

"Mereka tanya macam mana saya tahu. Saya secara berseloroh ingatkan mereka yang saya boleh dengar pengumuman. Mereka jawab, 'Oh lupa awak boleh dengar sebab awak selalu guna bahasa isyarat dengan kami.'"
Pengalaman seperti ini mendorong Wan Zuraidah untuk terus berkhidmat kepada golongan pekak, hampir tiga dekad selepas beliau mula bekerja di sebuah sekolah untuk kanak-kanak pekak.
"Setiap hari saya perlu tinggal sejam selepas waktu kerja semata-mata untuk belajar bahasa isyarat," katanya.

Sejak itu, Wan Zuraidah melihat kehidupan komuniti pekak daripada perspektif berbeza. Bagi beliau, cabaran mereka bukan terletak pada ketidakupayaan mendengar, tetapi jurang komunikasi dalam persekitaran.
"Kenapa tidak kita kongsi apa yang kita dengar dengan mereka? Mereka juga berhak tahu apa yang sedang berlaku di sekeliling," katanya.
Menurut statistik Jabatan Kebajikan Masyarakat, seramai 48,382 individu berdaftar di bawah kategori OKU pendengaran setakat 31 Mei 2025.
Persekutuan Orang Pekak Malaysia (MFD) percaya jumlah sebenar lebih tinggi kerana masih ramai yang belum didaftarkan, antaranya akibat kurang kesedaran dan stigma masyarakat.
"Bagi kami, perkataan 'pekak' seperti yang dijelaskan dalam Kamus Dewan hanya merujuk kepada seseorang yang tidak boleh mendengar dengan baik atau sepenuhnya.
"Ia bukan perkataan yang negatif. Yang perlu diubah ialah cara masyarakat melihat kami," kata Pengarah Eksekutif MFD, Mohamad Sazali Sha'ari, kepada FMT.

Sazali hilang pendengaran sepenuhnya ketika berusia 10 tahun akibat demam panas. Katanya, komuniti pekak bukan mengharapkan layanan istimewa, sebaliknya peluang untuk menjalani kehidupan seperti masyarakat lain.
Justeru, katanya, perubahan perlu bermula dengan kefahaman dan penerimaan masyarakat terhadap keperluan komuniti pekak.
"Kami cuma berbeza daripada segi komunikasi. Anda menggunakan komunikasi secara lisan, manakala kami menggunakan Bahasa Isyarat Malaysia," katanya.
Bagi meningkatkan kesedaran masyarakat, MFD akan menganjurkan sambutan Minggu Orang Pekak Antarabangsa secara besar-besaran pada 26 Sept ini di IWK Eco Park, Pantai Dalam, Kuala Lumpur.

Program itu menghimpunkan 50 usahawan pekak selain pameran perkhidmatan, kelas bahasa isyarat, khidmat nasihat kepada ibu bapa, dan pelbagai aktiviti interaktif yang memberi peluang kepada orang ramai memahami kehidupan komuniti tersebut.

"Sambutan ini bukan sekadar mempromosikan usahawan pekak, tetapi membuka ruang kepada masyarakat melihat sendiri kemampuan mereka apabila diberikan peluang dan sokongan yang sewajarnya”, kata Wan Zuraidah.

13f55a23f2413444: AICHI: Thailand's Puripol Boonson has set his sights on Su Bingtian's 100m record after opening his Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games campaign with a blistering 9.95 seconds on Thursday.
The 20-year-old came within 0.01 of his personal best to win his heat at Mizuo Park Athletic Stadium, producing the fastest time of the first round and sending an early warning to his rivals.
Puripol, the only Southeast Asian sprinter to have broken 10 seconds, now has the 9.92 Games record and Bingtian's Asian mark of 9.83 in his sights.
"So confident," said Puripol, who won silver at the Hangzhou Asian Games three years ago.
"I want to win a gold medal for Thailand because this year I'm really hoping for the 100m title," he told the medai after his race.
His sizzling run also caught the attention of Malaysia's Azeem Fahmi, who qualified third-fastest overall after winning his heat in 10.17.
But rather than being intimidated by Puripol's early burst, the 2022 Hangzhou bronze medallist wants to chase the Thai all the way in Friday's semi-finals and final.
"I don't think he has any pressure and I also don't have any pressure. I just want to run my own race and not think too much about what others are doing," said Azeem.

Azeem was satisfied with his opening run after achieving his initial target of reaching the semi-finals, but knows he will need to find more speed if he is to stay in the hunt for a place in the final.
"Today's race was quite good. Our target was just to execute the race well and make sure we qualify for the semi-finals. Tomorrow I will come back and try to do better," he said.
Puripol, who will also compete in the 200m and 4x100m, is chasing a sprint treble in Japan, while Azeem will be hoping his own chase can keep him within striking distance of the Thai favourite.

6c3a9f700face67b: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Malaysia’s Leading Index (LI) grew 1.1 per cent year-on-year in July 2026 to 115.3 points from 114.0 points in the same month last year, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM).

The department said the increase was mainly driven by real imports of other basic precious and other non-ferrous metals, which rose 24.1 per cent, and real imports of semiconductors, which increased 17.4 per cent. “Nonetheless, the overall performance softened slightly due to more moderate activity in several components, particularly the number of new companies registered,” it said in a statement today.

DOSM said although the smoothed long-term trend of the LI remained below 100.0 points, the domestic economic outlook is expected to remain resilient, strongly supported by a stable domestic labour market with a consistently low unemployment rate. “Furthermore, the influx of high-impact investments in high-tech sectors, alongside sustained global demand for the semiconductor ecosystem and electrical and electronics (E&E) products, serves as primary buffers to maintain Malaysia’s economic stability against external market uncertainties,” it added.
Meanwhile, the Coincident Index (CI), which reflects current economic developments, rose 1.7 per cent year-on-year to 131.5 points in July 2026 from 129.3 points in July 2025.
The growth was supported by a 5.8 per cent rise in real Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contributions, followed by a 4.5 per cent increase in the Industrial Production Index.

c48fa90c3aafbea9: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak could leave Kajang Prison as early as next month to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest if the High Court grants a stay of his 15-year 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) sentence, his lawyer Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah said today.
According to Utusan Malaysia, Shafee said the move could take place if the court grants the stay on October 14 and the RM50 million fine imposed as a condition of Najib’s conditional pardon is paid.
The High Court has fixed October 14 to hear Najib’s application to stay the execution of his 15-year prison sentence in the 1MDB case pending his appeal.

Asked how soon Najib could return home to serve his sentence under house arrest if all the required conditions were met, Shafee said it would depend on whether the necessary preparations had been completed.

“If we are ready, say on October 14 we obtain the stay of sentence and then, God willing, the RM50 million is paid, there is a strong possibility that he could be released on the same day,” he told reporters after court proceedings involving Najib.
“Or there may be arguments in court as to whether his release takes effect on the same day,” he said.
Shafee said the defence had sought the stay of the 1MDB sentence following the conditional pardon granted to Najib.
He said the legal team had previously not sought a stay when Najib was convicted in the 1MDB case because he was already serving his sentence for the SRC International case.
“However, the conditional pardon has changed the situation because the 1MDB sentence could affect Najib’s efforts to serve his SRC International sentence under house arrest,” he said.
“If the SRC sentence ends, the 1MDB sentence will begin, which is why we are seeking the stay, so that the stay has an effect,” he added.
Najib has appealed against his conviction and sentence on four charges of abusing his position and 21 money laundering charges involving RM2.27 billion in 1MDB funds.
The 15-year prison term imposed in the 1MDB case is to begin after he completes his sentence in the SRC International case.
61629c34c69e1e4d: Welcome to another edition of On Call, The Register’s reader-contributed Friday column that celebrates the unique workplace cultures that make delivering tech support such delightful fun. This week, meet a reader we’ll Regomize as “Antonio” who told us that in the late 1990s he worked for a multinational financial services organization. Not long after taking the job, Antonio was dispatched to Hong Kong to oversee the regional rollout of a new reverse proxy. Antonio gathered the local team for a town hall meeting at which he introduced himself to the 25-strong tech team who would work on the project. “I walked them through exactly what we were going to do and how everything had to be configured,” he explained to On Call. And then, cognizant that some on the team were more comfortable speaking Cantonese, he apologized for speaking in English for so long and asked if everyone understood the plan. “I was met with beaming faces and vigorously nodding heads,” Antonio told On Call. And with that, the team started work. “Implementation weekend came and went in a bit of a blur, but on Monday morning all sorts of weird things started to go wrong,” Antonio wrote. He looked into it and found configurations that were close to those he had put in the plan, but not quite perfect. “Key parts of our production environment - and elements on which we had dependencies, like load balancers, routers and so on, we're all ‘out of whack,” he told On Call. It took Antonio four days to figure out the problems and fix the mess. “I eventually pulled the team back together for a de-brief to figure out where things had gone wrong and why the production build had been subtly tweaked so that it appeared to comply with our plans but in fact did not.” A solemn-faced team member offered an explanation: “Our way is better.” Antonio responded without quite containing his incredulity. "Not better," he countered, "because the parts you changed broke.” He then reminded the team that he had asked if they understood the migration plan, and that everyone indicated they did. “So can you help me understand why you said you understood the plan and then did something else?" he asked. "We said we understood your plan,” came the response. “That was the question you asked, not whether we would follow it. Our plan was different. Our plan was better." Antonio said he tried to explain his point of view and eventually came to realize that when working abroad, understanding local culture can be as important as technical skill. Or as he put it to On Call: “Tech is easy. People are hard.” Have you struggled to make tech work across cultures? If so, click here to send your story to On Call so we can share it on a future Friday. ®
a8f9a3829d0bd2f8: PETALING JAYA: Bekas menteri besar Negeri Sembilan Aminuddin Harun menggesa Ismail Lasim berterus terang kepada rakyat dan menghentikan tuduhan menyalahkan 'kerajaan terdahulu' berhubung kemelut institusi diraja negeri itu.

Aminuddin berkata, Ismail perlu menjelaskan mengapa beliau menandatangani dokumen proklamasi berkaitan Yang Dipertuan Besar pada 3 Ogos lalu, sedangkan beliau sendiri menolak untuk menandatanganinya pada April atas faktor keraguan proses undang-undang.
Menurutnya, dokumen proklamasi bertarikh 19 April pernah dikemukakan kepadanya untuk ditandatangani mengikut Perkara 10 Undang-undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan (UUTKNS) 1959.

Namun, beliau membuat keputusan untuk tidak menandatanganinya selepas mendapati terdapat persoalan serius mengenai proses yang dilalui, termasuk isu pertikaian kedudukan salah seorang pihak yang terlibat sebagai Undang Luak Sungei Ujong.

“Persoalannya, jika saya ketika menjadi menteri besar boleh membuat keputusan untuk tidak menandatangani dokumen tersebut kerana mempunyai keraguan terhadap prosesnya, bagaimana pula tandatangan menteri besar selepas saya boleh berada pada dokumen yang sama?
“Inilah persoalan yang perlu dijelaskan secara terus kepada rakyat. Jangan sekadar menggunakan istilah ‘kerajaan terdahulu’ sebagai jawapan umum,” katanya di hantaran di Facebook.

Semalam, Ismail dalam satu sidang media berkata kemelut melibatkan institusi adat dan raja di Negeri Sembilan bukan berpunca daripada pentadbiran semasa tetapi diwarisi akibat kegagalan menteri besar terdahulu melaksanakan tanggungjawab mengikut UUTKNS.

Mengulas lanjut, Aminuddin turut menyatakan sokongan terhadap pendirian Jabatan Peguam Negara (AGC) pada 17 September lalu yang memutuskan bahawa proklamasi bertarikh 19 April adalah tidak sah kerana gagal mematuhi kehendak mandatori siasatan penuh di bawah Perkara 10 UUTKNS.
“AGC juga menegaskan bahawa menteri besar dan Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri tidak mempunyai kuasa secara unilateral untuk mengosongkan jawatan Yang Dipertuan Besar.

“Dalam perkara yang melibatkan UUTKNS, Adat Perpatih dan institusi Yang Dipertuan Besar, penjelasan kepada rakyat mestilah berasaskan fakta, proses dan rekod yang sebenar. Jangan lakukan manipulasi sekadar untuk melepaskan diri,” katanya.
91840481ae62488c: PETALING JAYA: Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama (SMKA) Jempol di Negeri Sembilan bakal menjadi sekolah aliran agama pendidikan dan latihan teknikal dan vokasional (TVET) pertama negara.
Menteri Pendidikan Fadhlina Sidek, berkata sekolah berkenaan dibina dengan kos RM98 juta di atas tapak seluas 14.22 hektar bagi tempoh tiga tahun menerusi Rancangan Malaysia Ke-12 (RMK-12).

0758f10a5194d7cb: SINGAPORE: The Singapore Food Agency (SFA) has initiated an investigation into an allegation of illegal dog meat sales posted on a social media platform.
The agency said it has not approved the sale of any dog meat and stressed that all food imports must meet SFA requirements in response to media queries on Friday.
A social media post shared on Wednesday on the Facebook group named 'Dogs Singapore' was believed to have promoted various dog meat dishes for sale to the public.The post has since been deleted.
SFA said illegally imported food products from unknown sources can pose a food safety risk.
"Meat and meat products can only be imported by licensed importers from SFA-accredited sources.
"It is an offence to sell meat and meat products that were imported without a valid licence or valid import permit," it said.
According to SFA, offenders found selling illegally imported meat and meat products are liable, upon conviction, to a jail term of up to two years, a fine of up to SG$50,000 (SG$1=RM3.19), or both.
Repeat offenders can be jailed for up to three years, fined up to SG$100,000, or both.

"While SFA puts in place and enforces regulatory measures, food importers and retailers must play their part by ensuring that the food products they bring into Singapore for sale comply with SFA's import requirements and are safe for consumption," it said.
0e1a7d0c16514b2c: PETALING JAYA: Former Negeri Sembilan menteri besar Aminuddin Harun today hit back at his successor, Ismail Lasim, for blaming the previous state administration for the ongoing crisis involving the state’s customary and royal institutions.
Ismail said yesterday the crisis was inherited from the previous state government, alleging that Aminuddin failed to fulfil his responsibilities under the state’s constitution.
In a statement, Aminuddin said the public should be told which constitutional provision the previous state administration was alleged to have violated.
"What action did I fail to take? What provision of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959 was breached, and when did the alleged breach occur?" he said.
"If there was a mistake, state what the mistake was. If there was a breach of the law, state the provision. In a matter of this magnitude, the people deserve clear and verifiable facts."
Aminuddin said he was prepared to be questioned about the matter, adding that his actions and decisions as menteri besar could be evaluated against the available records and documents.
Due process
He raised the issue of a proclamation dated April 19, saying it was presented to him for signing on April 20 while he was still menteri besar.
Aminuddin said the document was presented with reference to the process under Article 10 of the state constitution, but he decided not to sign it because of serious questions surrounding the process.

Article 10 of the state constitution governs the specific circumstances and procedures under which the Undang Yang Empat – the four ruling chieftains – may temporarily suspend or permanently remove the Yang Dipertuan Besar from the throne.

Aminuddin said Article 10 did not merely concern the powers relating to the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar, but also prescribed a process that had to be fulfilled, including matters relating to a full and complete inquiry.
He said there was also a dispute at the time over the position of one of the parties involved as the undang of Sungei Ujong.
"Ismail, as someone with a legal background, is certainly very familiar with the word ‘process’. Was it complete? Or was it flawed from the very beginning?" he said.

"In such circumstances, I took a position based on proper legal advice that a menteri besar should not put his signature on a document with such major implications for the royal institution while questions over its process and validity remained unclear.
"This was my position and, Alhamdulillah, that position remains unchanged today, and I do not consider myself to have been 'forced'."
Aminuddin also asked why Ismail signed the document when he had earlier refused to do so.

"If I, as menteri besar, could decide not to sign the document because I had doubts about the process, how could the signature of the menteri besar who came after me appear on the same document?" he said.
"This is the question that needs to be explained directly to the people."

Aminuddin also pointed to differing interpretations surrounding Article 10 of the state constitution. He said the provision should be treated as a constitutional process with specific requirements and procedures, including whether the requirement for a full and complete inquiry was fulfilled.

Aminuddin said the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) took the position on Sept 17 that the April 19 proclamation was invalid because the mandatory requirements under Article 10 were not complied with.
He said the AGC also maintained that the menteri besar and state executive council did not have unilateral power to declare the office of the Yang Dipertuan Besar vacant.
c7f72a96a1a57f41: KUALA LUMPUR: Kawan Renergy Bhd's margins may soon recover after cost overruns at its 52MW Sipitang, Sabah power plant project weighed on earnings in the second quarter of 2026.
Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) said the expected recovery in the third quarter of 2026 (Q3 FY26) will be supported by improved project execution and cost control.
PublicInvest analyst Khairul Fahmi said the overruns were largely one-off and project-specific.
This mainly stemmed from additional work beyond the initial scope and increased manpower deployment to mitigate project delays.

"Given the largely one-off and project-specific nature of these overruns, we expect margins to improve in Q3 FY26, although structural higher labour costs and incremental sales and service tax charges could limit the extent of the recovery," it said in a note.
PublicInvest retained its "Neutral" call on Kawan Renergy with an unchanged target price of RM0.51.
This is pending the company's upcoming results and greater clarity on margin normalisation.
Kawan Renergy had secured RM58 million worth of subcontract works from KAB Energy Holdings Sdn Bhd in August 2024.
They cover mechanical, firefighting and electrical works, with completion originally targeted for the first quarter of 2026.

The fixed lump-sum nature of the subcontract limited the company's ability to immediately recover the additional costs, with potential reimbursement still subject to variation claims and commercial settlement with the main contractor.

PublicInvest said Kawan Renergy took a conservative approach in Q2 FY26 by recognising provisions for foreseeable losses on the project while factoring in the probability of recovery, pending negotiations with the main contractor.

As a result, core profit after tax and minority interest (Patami) fell 91.3 per cent quarter-on-quarter and 89.9 per cent year-on-year to RM500,000, from RM5.5 million in Q2 FY26 and RM4.8 million in Q2 FY25.
The firm expects Kawan Renergy's core Patami to recover in the second half of FY26, forecasting RM7.7 million compared with RM6 million in the first half.
Separately, Kawan Renergy secured approval from the Sustainable Energy Development Authority (Seda) in August 2026 for a 2.5MW biomass power plant under a 21-year Feed-in Tariff (FiT) arrangement.
The plant, which has a net export capacity of 2MW, is scheduled to commence commercial operations on Aug 17, 2029.
The approved basic tariff is 38 sen per kilowatt-hour for the first 10 years, before declining to 28.8 sen per kWh for the remaining 11 years.
PublicInvest said the project would broaden Kawan Renergy's recurring income base, although its earnings contribution is expected to remain marginal.
It estimated the plant would contribute about RM1 million in PAT, equivalent to 0.18 sen in earnings per share, in its first full year of operations in FY30.
As the contribution falls outside its current earnings forecast period, the firm made no changes to its earnings forecasts or valuation.

4153ead586ee5fc5: NEW YORK: Malaysia menggesa perkongsian beban dan tanggungjawab antarabangsa yang lebih besar bagi menyokong negara-negara yang menempatkan pelarian Rohingya susulan konflik berpanjangan dan keadaan kemanusiaan yang meruncing di Myanmar.

“Perkongsian beban dan tanggungjawab antarabangsa yang lebih besar amat diperlukan bagi menyokong negara-negara yang menempatkan pelarian Rohingya,” kata beliau ketika menyampaikan intervensi pada Mesyuarat Penyelarasan Tahunan Menteri-Menteri Luar OIC di ibu pejabat Pertubuhan Bangsa-Bangsa Bersatu (PBB).

Mohamad berkata Malaysia kekal komited terhadap usaha memastikan pertanggungjawaban atas pelanggaran hak asasi manusia dan menyokong kes yang dikemukakan Gambia terhadap Myanmar di Mahkamah Keadilan Antarabangsa (ICJ).

“Mengekalkan saluran komunikasi amat penting bagi memajukan keterangkuman, menangani kebimbangan dan membina keyakinan ke arah keamanan serta kestabilan berkekalan.

“Dengan mengambil kira perkara itu, Malaysia menyertai Kumpulan Hubungan OIC mengenai Afghanistan pada Februari 2026 dan berharap dapat memberikan sumbangan konstruktif kepada usaha berkenaan,” kata beliau.
Mohamad kini berada di New York dari 23 hingga 27 Sept bagi mengetuai delegasi Malaysia ke sesi ke-81 Perhimpunan Agung PBB (UNGA).

d090c77c2f321a48: PUTRAJAYA: An academic has called for a dedicated commission to strengthen governance and integrity in Malaysia's crowdfunding and fundraising sectors.

Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia (USIM) Faculty of Economics and Muamalat associate professor Dr Muhammad Iqmal Hisham Kamaruddin said the recommendation stems from his study addressing regulatory gaps and overlapping functions among existing authorities.
Presenting his findings at the Fifth National Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption Research Conference 2026 today, he outlined three regulatory models proposed in the study.
"The first model would establish a commission with full registration and regulatory functions by consolidating existing authorities' roles.
"The second would create a commission with specific regulatory functions while leaving registration with existing bodies.
"The third option would form a council or committee to coordinate regulatory functions if the government decides against a standalone commission."
Iqmal said the first model was the preferred approach as it consolidates the functions of three relevant authorities into a single agency, eliminating overlapping powers regarding public funds.
He added that the commission was needed due to regulatory gaps caused by the lack of a specific law governing crowdfunding as a whole.
The study identified overlapping functions involving public funds among the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU), Registrar of Societies (RoS) and Companies Commission of Malaysia (SSM).

Under the proposed framework, the commission could require organisations to obtain approval before raising public funds, while overseeing financial reporting, audits, disclosures and other governance requirements.
The study also recommended introducing a dedicated Charities Act or Crowdfunding Act, a governance framework, entity classification based on size and funds raised, and a potential rating system.

Other proposals included digitalised record-keeping, integrated reporting among authorities, security screening for trustees, external audit support for smaller non-profit organisations and NGOs, stronger enforcement powers, and monitoring of crowdfunding promotions.
Iqmal added that the commission could oversee professional certification and training in crowdfunding governance, establish an industry association or council, and conduct public awareness campaigns.
The study involved a survey of 1,000 respondents nationwide, five focus group discussions with stakeholders, and an engagement session with three relevant authorities.

8a049835b9a70bbf: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 25 — Malaysia announced the establishment of the Malaysia-Indonesia Halal Council in a bid to strengthen halal diplomacy between the two countries, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today.

He added that the council would be chaired by Indonesia's Halal Product Assurance Organising Agency (BPJPH) with Malaysia serving as its secretary-general, and the first meeting would be held in October this year.

"Next month, the focus is on facilitating halal certification between Malaysia and Indonesia to ease bilateral halal trade between the two countries," he said in his speech at the Global Halal Summit 2026 here today.

Ahmad Zahid said the council would build on existing bilateral cooperation between Malaysia and Indonesia to address differing halal requirements, repeated procedures and difficulties faced by businesses seeking to enter neighbouring markets.

Malaysia and Indonesia signed a memorandum of cooperation in 2023, while bilateral negotiations on facilitating halal certification and trade between the two countries were concluded in June this year, he said.
He said closer bilateral cooperation could identify practical ways to facilitate trade, reduce duplication and connect businesses to regional supply chains.

Ahmad Zahid said Malaysia brings experience in standards, governance, Islamic finance and trade facilitation, while Indonesia offers scale, production capacity and entrepreneurship, which are at the core of halal diplomacy, where both parties can leverage the trust built to open markets, facilitate investment and create opportunities together.
He added that such cooperation should ultimately translate into fewer barriers, easier market access and more companies trading across borders.
He said small manufacturers should have a clearer route to overseas buyers, while halal-certified companies should receive the support needed to fulfil their first export orders.

"The future of halal will depend on how effectively we connect ourselves and build that trust in the future,” he said, adding that Malaysia aims to increase its halal exports to about RM80 billion by 2030.
Ahmad Zahid noted that the halal industry contributed about 11 per cent to Malaysia’s gross domestic product, yet only about 14.7 per cent of halal-certified companies were exporters.

"To realise our ambition, we must help more of these companies compete abroad. Certification is only the beginning of that journey. Companies also need consistent production, suitable packaging, working capital, reliable logistics and an understanding of their target markets,” he added.
Meanwhile, Ahmad Zahid shared that the International Halal Showcase (MIHAS) 2026 has attracted US$1.2 billion in sales over the first two days.
Hosted by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry and organised by the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation, MIHAS 2026 is being held from Sept 23 to Sept 26, 2026.

Ahmad Zahid hopes that sales and sales potential will continue to increase until MIHAS ends on Sunday, as the annual organisation of MIHAS has established the event as a global halal exhibition brand, despite several countries also organising similar exhibitions. — Bernama
797259737c83fa17: DUBLIN: Irish superstars U2 revealed the name of their new album on Wednesday – Carnaval de Luz – days ahead of the 50th anniversary of their first encounter as schoolboys in a Dublin kitchen in 1976.

"I can't say it. I'm going to say it," Bono teased on an Irish Times podcast which looked back on their career.
"The new album is called Carnaval de Luz ... it's strong stuff," Bono added while reminiscing about the four-piece band's formation in the kitchen of drummer Larry Mullen.

That seminal moment in rock history on Sept 25, 1976, is set to be celebrated during a U250 event organised by fans in Dublin this weekend, as well as with a new two euro coin issued by the Central Bank of Ireland on Friday.
The new album and the half-century anniversary underline the longevity of one of Ireland's biggest musical exports.
The landmark also begs questions about the secret of their success, which has seen the band outlast their peers, avoid messy break-ups, and continue to fill stadiums.
REINVENTION

While they could barely play their instruments at their first teenage rehearsal and nearly lost their record contract after a disappointing reception for second album "October", they went on to produce some of the biggest hits of the 1980s and 90s.
In total, they are estimated to have sold 175 million albums and count more than 23 million monthly listeners on Spotify today.
"Every album, they keep pushing creative boundaries," Alex Conyngham, owner of Slane Castle in Ireland, where the band have performed and recorded at several times over their career, told AFP.
"That's always been in their DNA. They've never been a band that have just rested on the hits."
The new album – the first since 2017's "Songs of Experience" – follows the release of new music this year including "Street of Dreams" in July.
Aidan Alcock, director of Dublin's famous Windmill Lane recording studios, where U2 recorded their debut album "Boy" and its two successors, also paid tribute to their ability to keep moving.
"They're always full of surprises. And I think that's what keeps them going as well," he told AFP.
Bono told the Irish Times that a drive for perfection served as his motivation, as well as the pleasure of hanging out with the band.

"I suppose it's always the thought that just around the corner lies the perfect song or the perfect performance ... it's mad to say but that's still the drug of choice in our band," he told the paper.
'SOFT POWER'
Composed of Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton, and Larry Mullen, U2 have become symbols of Ireland's rich musical culture and history, but also some of the best-known faces of the country overseas.

At an exhibition celebrating their 50 years together in Paris on Tuesday, the Irish ambassador to France, Alison Milton, paid tribute to them as "part of our reputation, our 'soft power' in international relations."
Exhibition curator Clement Mathieu, a journalist at Paris Match celebrity magazine, put U2's broad international appeal down to a hit-making record which rivals Michael Jackson or Madonna.
But also their character.

"There's something of the Irish soul in them: there's passion, there's love, there's anger. U2's music isn't particularly marked by an Irish sound; it's more marked by the Irish soul and the Irish heart," he told AFP.
With a new album, U2 will almost certainly hit the road again for a string of stadium concerts, another key part of their enduring appeal.
"They're one of the great performing bands," Conyngham told AFP.
"If you go to a U2 gig, you're never going to be disappointed in terms of the energy and commitment that they show up with. They're really hardworking."
